q: Does a lower clinker ratio cut a Turkish cement exporter's CBAM cost?
title: Turkish cement: clinker ratio and CBAM
short: Yes, with actual data. Clinker carries most of a cement's embedded emissions, so a blended cement with less clinker per tonne has a lower figure. Default values are set per CN code and do not reward blending, so the saving reaches the buyer only through verified actual emissions.
audience: Cement producers in Turkey shipping blended and Portland cement to EU buyers

sections.h: Why the ratio drives the number
p: Each tonne of clinker carries calcination CO2 and kiln fuel CO2. Cement's embedded emissions are roughly clinker share times clinker intensity, plus grinding electricity and any additives' emissions.
Default values apply per CN code and country. A CEM II or CEM III with 65% clinker and a CEM I with 95% fall under similar codes, so only actual data shows the gap.
Clinker consumed per cement type, additive purchases and electricity by mill. These let the verifier attribute emissions per product.

example.title: Illustrative embedded emissions per tonne of cement
lines: CEM I: 0.95 t clinker x 0.85 t CO2 = 0.81 t CO2
CEM II: 0.70 t clinker x 0.85 t CO2 = 0.60 t CO2
Add grinding electricity to each; the clinker share drives the gap
example.note: Clinker intensity is illustrative; use your plant's measured figure.
